name: Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥusayn ibn Aḥmad ibn Khālawayh
summary: Grammarian and reader of Hamadhān who studied in Baghdad and taught at the Ḥamdānid court of Aleppo; author of the grammatical analysis of thirty sūras and of a book on 'what is not found in the speech of the Arabs'.
bio: Ibn Khālawayh was born in Hamadhān and studied in Baghdad with Ibn Durayd, Nifṭawayh, Abū Bakr ibn al-Anbārī and Abū ʿUmar al-Zāhid, and the readings of the Qurʾān with Ibn Mujāhid. He settled in Aleppo, where Sayf al-Dawla gave him his sons to teach; the sources tell of his quarrels at that court with the poet al-Mutanabbī and with Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī.

His Iʿrāb thalāthīn sūra analyses word by word the thirty short sūras from al-Ṭāriq to the end of the Qurʾān and al-Fātiḥa, a model for later teaching; his Laysa fī kalām al-ʿarab collects the rare forms of which he could say 'there is nothing else like it in Arabic'. He also wrote on the seven readings and the irregular ones. He died in Aleppo in 370/980.
